issues.claim: Дополнительно: событие можно объявить в интерфейсе, а поле нельзя.
issues.problem: Imprecise. Since C# 8 an interface may contain static fields, so the true statement is that an interface cannot contain instance fields. The EN text has the same imprecision ("a field cannot").
issues.suggestedFix: RU: "событие можно объявить в интерфейсе, а поле экземпляра нельзя". EN: "an event can be declared in an interface, an instance field cannot".

issues.claim: Для поле-подобного события компилятор создаёт приватное поле-делегат и методы доступа `add` и `remove`
issues.problem: "поле-подобное" is unnatural Russian. The established term is "событие, подобное полю". The same wording appears in the third bullet ("поле-подобное событие базового класса").
issues.suggestedFix: "Для события, подобного полю, компилятор создаёт ..." and "вызвать событие базового класса, подобное полю".

issues.claim: Even a derived class cannot invoke a field-like event of its base class
issues.problem: The claim is true (the compiler reports CS0070 in a derived class). However, the fetched excerpt of the cited event page says events can be invoked "from within the class (or derived classes)", which reads as the opposite. The excerpt supports only the protected virtual OnXxx pattern, through a code comment in its sample. A reader checking the source could be confused.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a sentence to the explanation: "Despite loose wording in some docs, a derived class cannot invoke a field-like event of its base class (CS0070), so the base class exposes a protected OnChanged method."

issues.problem: The URL redirects to csharp-version-history#c-version-12 and the page title is "The history of C#". So link 1 and link 3 point to the same page, and the title "What's new in C# 12" does not match the fetched page.
issues.suggestedFix: Drop the third link (csharp-version-history) and its linkTitles entries. Alternatively, point link 1 at csharp-version-history#c-version-12 and retitle it "История версий C#" / "The history of C#".

issues.claim: Before that, the `Type(...)` syntax after the type name existed only for records (C# 9).
issues.problem: Imprecise. Record structs (C# 10) also had positional syntax. The same applies to the RU option explanation c, where "C# 12 only extended this syntax to ordinary classes and structs" overlooks record structs, and to the RU explanation.
issues.suggestedFix: "existed only for records and record structs (C# 9 and C# 10)"; apply the same change in RU.
